content.text:
Notely now sends a welcome email when a user is created and a password reset email on request, both through **Resend**. Lint and build pass. I ran a smoke test of the whole flow with no API key set, so emails were printed to the console instead of sent. Nothing has gone through Resend for real yet, and nothing is committed.

**Why Resend:** it fits Next.js on serverless hosting, has a simple API and a free tier, and has good deliverability. I call its REST API directly with `fetch`, so there's no new dependency.

**What's new**
- `src/lib/email/send.ts`: `sendEmail()`. In development without `RESEND_API_KEY`, it prints the email to the server console. In production, a missing key throws an error.
- `src/lib/email/templates.ts`: the welcome and reset emails, each with an HTML and a plain-text version. User-supplied values are escaped in the HTML.
- `.env.example`: `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM` and `APP_URL`, with placeholder values. I also added `!.env.example` to `.gitignore`, because the existing `.env*` rule would have hidden the file.
- `README.md`: the status section now describes the email setup.

**Changes in `src/lib/users.ts`**
- `users.ts` had no way to create users, so I added **`createUser({ email, name, password? })`**. It lowercases the email, rejects duplicates and sends the welcome email. If the email fails to send, it's logged and the account is still created.
- **`requestPasswordReset(email)`** emails a single-use link to `/reset-password?token=…` that expires after 60 minutes. Only a hash of the token is stored, and a new request cancels older links. It behaves the same whether or not the email belongs to an account, so it can't be used to check who has one.
- **`resetPassword(token, newPassword)`** checks and uses up the token, then saves the new password hash.
- Supporting functions: `getUserByEmail` and `verifyPassword`. Passwords are hashed with scrypt and kept apart from `User`, so `listUsers()` never exposes them.

The smoke test confirmed that both emails are created, a reset works, a reused token is rejected, the new password works and the old one doesn't, unknown emails get no email, and duplicate users are rejected.

**Still missing**
- **No reset page:** there's no `/reset-password` page or sign-up page yet, so nothing in the app calls these functions so far. The reset page just needs to call `resetPassword(token, password)`.
- **Lost on restart:** users, password hashes and reset tokens are all kept in memory and disappear when the server restarts. A real database is needed before production.
- **Before sending for real:** verify a sending domain in Resend and set `EMAIL_FROM` to an address on it. Until then, Resend only lets you send to your own account's address.
